correctness.rationale: The wheel mixture identity follows from the hub-first event, and the gear identity from the hub arriving before the first accepted even rim site. A disjoint-triples estimate and short-time union bound show gear hub acceptance probability asymptotic to λ/m. Factorially decaying descending-clock causal paths and an R-dependent fourth-moment bound give o(m^-1) baseline concentration, sufficient to condition on that rare hub event. The first two moment identities then yield the four stated limits. The base one-dimensional variance coefficient e^-4 per site is established in Penrose–Sudbury (2005), Theorem 11, transferred to a cycle by finite-moment causal locality; not inferred from finite data. The actual packaged verify.py passed exact finite arithmetic tests and 10,400 checked equalities/inequalities and orderwise couplings.

value.rationale: A physically natural local topology change produces opposite sign order-one expected coverage shifts but same-sign O(m) variance amplification. This isolates a rare early hub deposition event of probability Θ(1/m) that can alter Θ(m) future deposits, demonstrating how a single diverging-degree defect changes fluctuations in a one-dimensional jammed gas. The result supplies explicit all-rate coefficients and a contrasting wheel/gear benchmark, not a routine finite table entry.
